items.snippet: Projects feel meaningful; homework repeats the same pattern every week.
I prefer when we do something practical, not just answering questions from the textbook.
Group projects are nice because you can share ideas and divide work.
Working in groups makes class way more fun, especially when we get to pick our own teams.
I get nervous presenting but I think it helps me be more confident over time.
Some kids don't do their share in group work and that's really frustrating.
The workshops are the best part. You actually build things and see how they work.
Theory lessons can be boring but I understand why we need them for the exams.
My favourite class is the one where we design circuits. It feels like real engineering.
The language apps are cool but my eyes get tired after using them for too long.
I like real books better. You can highlight things and flip back easily.
We use tablets every day now. It's convenient but sometimes the wifi doesn't work.
The routine was hard at first but now I actually like having a clear schedule.
Discipline teaches you to focus. I think I'm better at studying because of it.
Some rules feel unnecessary but overall the structure helps me manage my time.
Exam stress is real. Sometimes I can't sleep the night before a big test.
Study groups really help because you can explain things to each other.
My teacher gives us a revision plan and that makes it less overwhelming.
I was really scared on the first day. Everything was so big and different.
Making new friends was hard but after a few weeks it got better.
The homework is way more than primary school. I had to learn how to plan my time.
